newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer backed by palladium.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer backed by palladium.

text.p: Precious metals prices were markedly firmer on Thursday with buying in palladium, believed to be on behalf of a fund, the driving factor, dealers said.
Palladium has rebounded from $141.48 per ounce on March 18 back up to $151.50/$152.50 at 1000 GMT and dealers said the aggressive buying had come mostly from one fund.

Dealers said palladium's background was dominated by the delay in shipments between the largest exporter Russia and Japan the biggest importer, and a likely strike at Russia's Norilsk mining and refining centre.
Gold was fixed at $352.70 per ounce up from $349.10 on Wednesday afternoon and a close of $348.70/$349.20.
"Europe has been fairly quiet so far as the market has been fund driven. All eyes will be on that again today," one dealer said.

Gold and silver had seen very good physical offtake at the lower levels this week which had helped to stabilise the markets and provide a floor at $346-$348 and $5.09-$5.12 respectively, dealers said.
They noted that lease rates had come off again after rising earlier in the week indicating that a move to rebuild short positions had not been followed through.
Even so gold was unlikely to climb through the $355.00 resistance level on Thursday and trading would be slanted towards the over-the-counter (OTC) option expiry next Tuesday.
"Recently there has been rallies after expiries as option writers have moved to cover naked calls," one dealer noted.
Short covering on Wednesday also helped gold's recovery, dealers said. However the main dynamic behind the market was coming from the white metals, especially palladium.
"With Russia being such a dominant supplier (about 60 percent of world demand is met by Russia exports), there is more scope for manipulation," one dealer said.
However he noted that at previous peaks -- when palladium approached $160 recently -- consumers had been willing to look to nickel and other cheaper materials as substitutes.
Palladium prices have risen about 34 percent from their recent low of around $117.00 in early January.
Platinum was at $378.75/$379.75 up $2.50 and would encounter technical resistance at $381.00, technical analysts said.

However a move through that could take it to recent highs at $391.00 and $393.00, but according to recent experience, a fall would be caught at $370.00 which one analyst said was a buying opportunity.
